Build items by substituting categories into one question stem

template_items.Rd

Turns a list of categories into the questions for an instrument of independent binary items. The category goes into the question, not the answer, so categories may be any length and the tokenization constraint never applies.

Usage

template_items(stem, categories, lang = c("en", "es"), medium = NULL)

Arguments

stem

A named stem, or a custom string containing {label}.

categories

A character vector of categories. Names, if present, become item names.

lang

A string giving the language for the named stems, "en" (the default) or "es". Ignored for a custom string, which is used exactly as written. This sets the question only. The scaffolding around it is instrument()'s own lang, and leaving that at its default gives a Spanish question under an English cue.

medium

A string naming the stem set a named stem is looked up in, one of "text", "audio", "image" or "video". Read only for a named stem, since a custom string carries its own wording. There is no default, because the sets differ by medium rather than translating, so a default would answer a question about the document with a guess.

Value

A named list of questions, one per category, ready to pass to instrument() as its first argument.

Names are the names of categories, so they become the item names in the results and in item_report(). Pass a named vector to control them. An unnamed vector uses the values themselves, which rarely suits a category that runs to a phrase.

Values are the stem with {label} replaced by each category's text. Order is preserved, and an instrument reads in the order its items were declared rather than alphabetically.

The result is an ordinary list, so an item can be edited before it reaches instrument() when one category needs wording the stem cannot give it.

The named stems

Four sets, one per medium, each in English and in Spanish. medium picks the set and lang picks the language.

mediumstems
"text"topic, mention, express, about, frame
"audio"topic, mention, express, about, frame
"image"show, depict, express, about, frame
"video"show, depict, discuss, express, about, frame

The sets are not translations of one another, which is why medium has no default.

The text set in full. The other three take the same shape with their own noun and their own verbs.

stemenes
"topic"Does this text discuss {label}?¿Este texto trata sobre {label}?
"mention"Does this text mention {label}?¿Este texto menciona {label}?
"express"Does this text express {label}?¿Este texto expresa {label}?
"about"Is this text primarily about {label}?¿Este texto trata principalmente de {label}?
"frame"Does this text frame the issue in terms of {label}?¿Este texto enmarca el tema en términos de {label}?

These differ in what they assert, not in topic. "mention" fires on a passing reference. "about" requires the text to be centrally concerned with the category. The choice is a measurement decision, and it is the same decision in either language, since the two halves of a row are translations of one another rather than separate instruments.

A custom string ignores lang entirely, so a Spanish question written by hand is passed through as typed. The scaffolding around it is a separate setting, on instrument(), and the two can disagree. See its lang argument.

See also

instrument(), which takes the items.

Examples

template_items("topic", c(econ = "the economy", immig = "immigration"),
               medium = "text")
#> $econ
#> [1] "Does this text discuss the economy?"
#> 
#> $immig
#> [1] "Does this text discuss immigration?"
#> 

# The same stem name asks a different question of a different document.
template_items("about", c(econ = "the economy"), medium = "image")
#> $econ
#> [1] "Is this image primarily about the economy?"
#> 

# A custom string carries its own wording, so it needs no medium.
template_items("Does the author appear to endorse {label}?", c("austerity"))
#> $austerity
#> [1] "Does the author appear to endorse austerity?"
#>
